title: Stability island: staging pacing, cohort throttles, and rehydration notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick, messy notebook of ideas for a staging-first release flow that minimizes cold-cache-induced latency spikes. This is a personal runbook / working doc: not yet formalized. Use to iterate with SRE + runtime team.

High-level idea (stability island):
- Ship new model/version into an isolated cohort ring that gets a small steady stream of production traffic but with explicit priming sequences to rehydrate KV caches and model weights on GPUs.
- Control admission with per-cohort throttles and a pacing ramp that adapts to observed median P95 token latency and error budget consumption.
- If cold spikes occur, we have two escape hatches: immediate pinback to previous model for affected tenants OR force-warm via synthetic priming traffic to specific nodes.

Why this shape?
- Pure canary (tiny traffic % without priming) often shows good correctness signals but hides performance regressions until ramping up.
- Full warmup in staging avoids surprises in critical paths: user-facing latency regressions are the hardest to detect late.

Staging cohort topology (proposal):
- Island-0 (priming-only): 0.5% global qps, synthetic priming traffic only, no user-visible responses. Purpose: get weights + KV warmed.
- Island-1 (shadow + small live): 1% global qps, shadowed responses for all traffic but 0.5% live randomized users across low-risk tenants.
- Island-2 (expanded): 5% qps, targeted to mid-risk tenants with monitoring hooks.
- Steady-state flows into Dedicated/Host pools after verification.

Pacing & throttle heuristics (initial):
- Ramp window: conservative 30m per stage on average; accelerate to 10m if P95 latency delta < +10% and error rate within baseline.
- Admission throttle: set token-per-second cap per cohort (start small, increase by 2x each successful window).
- Warmup sequencing: seed Node-level KV with 10 representative prompt prefixes from the tenant (if available) + 20 generic prefixes from global corpora; run 3x back-to-back to ensure KV is resident.

Metrics to watch (primary):
- P50/P95/P99 token latency (per model + per cohort)
- 4xx/5xx error rates and model-quality errors (malformed tokenization, RNG failures)
- Per-request kg (cost per token) and GPU utilization per node
- Cache hit ratio for KV cache (prefix-level)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) as proxy for cold path
- Customer-facing errors (from Sentry) bucketed by tenant

Automated guards (alerts):
- P95 delta > +25% over baseline for 5m -> pause admissions and open incident channel
- Error rate > 0.5% absolute increase -> auto-pin to previous version for affected cohort (manual review for full rollbacks)
- GPU mem pressure > 90% with rising OOM events -> stop priming and throttle cohort to 0.1% until healthy

Manual checks (pre-stage checklist):
- Confirm training artifacts hash matches model catalog entry (model_id / commit).
- Validate quantization profile applied (if using q4/q5) — run small deterministic inference vector checks.
- Run smoke suite with 50 synthetic prompts, record outputs and hashes.
- Create cohort routing rule in control plane and mark with "stability-island" tag.
- Notify on-call SRE and runtime lead with expected time window and telemetry dashboard links.

Priming recipe (practical commands & notes):
- Use priming-worker (repo script): priming-worker --model model:v2 --nodes 4 --prefixes-file tenants/seed-prefixes.txt --reps 3 --delay 5s
- If nodes are in warm-state but KV low, run targeted short-run with heavier prefix multiplicity: --reps 6 --burst-size 20
- Keep priming at low concurrency to avoid saturating CPU tokenizers.

Rollback & rescue playbook (fast):
- Trigger: any P95 delta > +50% OR sustained 5xx spike for 10m.
- Steps: 1) Pause cohort routing (API call: /admin/cohort/{id}/pause) 2) Pin traffic to previous model on cohort: /admin/models/pin -> prev-model:stable 3) Scale down new-model allocation (node drain) and add to maintenance schedule. 4) If pin fails, open immediate incident and execute global fallback route (route to hosted-readonly).
- Quick commands (notes-to-self):
  - curl -XPOST $CTRLPLANE/cohorts/put -d '{"id":"island-1","state":"paused"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  - redis-cli HSET model-routing island-1 prev_model v1.4.2

Telemetry & dashboarding (what to build next):
- Cohort live diff view: compare cohort-to-cohort P95 and error rate side-by-side with annotation of priming windows.
- Heatmap of TTFT vs KV hit ratio by node.
- Lightweight quality regression detector that compares top-k outputs for a small eval set (non-PII).

Open questions / things to experiment with:
- How much synthetic priming traffic is enough? Proposal: calibrate by measuring incremental KV hit ratio per 100 priming requests. Goal: reach >80% KV hit for representative prefixes.
- Tenant-aware priming: should we only prime tenants that will be routed to the cohort, or prime generically and accept mismatch? Tradeoff: privacy and cost.
- Can we reuse prewarmed nodes across sequential model flips to reduce churn? Risk: mixing model kernels and quantization caches.
- Can a short-term microservice act as an admission mediator to smooth bursts into island cohorts?

Notes to self (rough):
- Try this flow on the low-risk integration tenant ("playground-inc") next week. Ask Priya for their top-10 prefixes.
- Evan: can you sketch a minimal dashboard that shows cohort delta over last 60 minutes? Put link in linked_artifacts.
- If we see steady TTFT > 400ms during priming, consider increasing priming reps rather than cohort pause.

Todo (action items):
- [ ] Draft a formal SRE runbook from this notebook (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Run a dry-run with priming-worker against staging cluster (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Create small eval set for quick quality smoke tests (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Add automated guard to pause admissions on P95 delta > 25% (owner: SRE)
notes_summary: Working notebook for a "stability island" staged deployment flow emphasizing priming/rehydration, cohort throttles, and fast rollback playbooks. Draft/experiment stage.
